blog_summary: Adrian Colyer highlights a 2018 VAST paper that explores the real-world practices of professional data analysts during exploratory data analysis (EDA). The study, based on interviews with 30 experienced analysts, reveals that EDA is an open-ended, informal process aimed at uncovering insights, generating hypotheses, and guiding further analysis. Colyer notes the paper's emphasis on the 'futzing and moseying' nature of EDA, where analysts engage in exploratory, iterative activities like data wrangling, profiling, and visualization. Key challenges include high overheads in data preparation, lack of clear goals from clients, and difficulties in tracking data versions and analysis provenance. The paper also discusses the tools analysts use, with SQL databases, spreadsheets, and Jupyter notebooks being the most common, and expresses a desire for integrated environments combining notebooks with interactive visualizations. Colyer points out that while the study's findings may have evolved with newer tools, the core challenges and motivations in EDA remain relevant.
paper_title: Futzing and moseying: interviews with professional data analysts on exploration practices
paper_abstract: —We report the results of interviewing thirty professional data analysts working in a range of industrial, academic, and regulatory environments. This study focuses on participants’ descriptions of exploratory activities and tool usage in these activities. Highlights of the findings include: distinctions between exploration as a precursor to more directed analysis versus truly open-ended exploration; confirmation that some analysts see “finding something interesting” as a valid goal of data exploration while others explicitly disavow this goal; conflicting views about the role of intelligent tools in data exploration; and pervasive use of visualization for exploration, but with only a subset using direct manipulation interfaces. These findings provide guidelines for future tool development, as well as a better understanding of the meaning of the term “data exploration” based on the words of practitioners “in the wild.” Index Terms—EDA, exploratory data analysis, interview study, visual analytics tools
